extracted.intended_audience: artists, architects, art historians, and educated readers interested in aesthetic theory
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating grotesque in art and architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for recognizing, judging, and producing the 'grotesque' in visual art and architecture, distinguishing noble invention from barbarous or base grotesque and situating those judgments in cultural, moral, and technical contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source: terror and contemplation of death
rubrics_metrics.description: The grotesque ... arises out of that condition of mind which appears to follow naturally upon the contemplation of death, and in which the fancy is brought into morbid action by terror, accompanied by the belief in spiritual presence, and in the possibility of spiritual apparition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emotional source produces the grotesque's most sublime, least voluntary creations; natural phenomena associated with death and the ghastliness of the skeleton feed grotesque invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noble grotesque requires appreciation of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The noble grotesque involves the true appreciation of beauty, though the mind may willfully turn to other images or stop short of perfection; whereas the grotesque of the Sandwich islander involves no perception or imagination of anything above itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grotesque results from an incapability of perceiving beauty it becomes savage or barbarous; many intermediate stages exist where gross or ludicrous images mingle with solemn subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque as marker of imaginative health and greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the human mind is healthy and vigorous in all its proportions ... there the grotesque will exist in full energy; there is no test of greatness in periods, nations, or men more sure than the development ... of a noble grotesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence and quality of grotesque invention as an index of the imaginative balance and greatness of individuals (Dante, Michelangelo, Tintoret) and cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of imagination, emotion, and intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: Great in imagination and emotion no less than in intellect, and not overborne by an undue or hardened preeminence of the mere reasoning faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grotesque flourishes where imaginative and emotional faculties are strong as well as intellectual ones; an overdominant rationalism quells grotesque invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention as test of grotesque quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Our power of judging of the rank of a grotesque work will depend on the degree in which we are in general sensible of the presence of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare inventive examples (e.g., Veronese Gothic lion head) with late ornamental pieces 'utterly devoid of invention' (e.g., Palazzo Corner boss) to judge rank; invention (originality, creative insight) is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution style: spirited sketching vs neat over-working
rubrics_metrics.description: The noble workman has used his chisel like a painter's pencil, and sketched the glory with a few irregular lines ... while the poor wretch ... was half a day in smoothing its vapid and vermicular curls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spontaneous, painterly, bold execution (leaving broken edges, decisive strokes) supports noble grotesque; overly neat, mechanical finishing can make grotesque merely abominable and lifeless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence in national mind beyond visible art
rubrics_metrics.description: It by no means follows that because the grotesque does not appear in the art of a nation, the sense of it does not exist in the national mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess national grotesque also via customs, festivals, gestures, and popular expression (e.g., Venetian ceremonies, acted grotesques) not only formal architectural or pictorial works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish grotesque from mere levity or pursuit of pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that we should carefully distinguish between it and the spirit of mere levity ... one thing to indulge in playful rest, and another to be devoted to the pursuit of pleasure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noble playful grotesque arises from deep seriousness and conscientious energy; continual pursuit of pleasure produces base, bitter, or foolish grotesque. Evaluate moral/psychological source when judging tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque's double moral effect (ennobling and degrading)
rubrics_metrics.description: These [grotesque images], partly degrading us by the instinctive and paralyzing terror with which they are attended, and partly ennobling us by leading our thoughts to dwell in the eternal world, fill the last and the most important circle ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that grotesque works can both horrify and uplift; assess which effect predominates and whether the work leads thought toward the eternal (ennobling) or merely paralyzes (degrading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and cultural conditions shape grotesque development
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of that grotesque took place under different laws from those which regulate it in any other European city. For ... the Byzantine mind ... was marked ... by the absence of the grotesque element ... and ... the Renaissance laws altogether checked its imagination in architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider local cultural, historical, and institutional influences (e.g., Byzantine, Lombard, Renaissance constraints) when explaining why grotesque appears or is suppressed in a region or period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between societal seriousness/conscientiousness and grotesque expression
rubrics_metrics.description: When serious, religious, and sincere ... the spirit of the noble grotesque not showing itself in art at all, but only in speech and action; in the second case, developing itself in painting, through accessories and vivacities of composition, while perfect dignity was always preserved in portraiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish social phases: a people may express grotesque in conduct and custom when morally earnest, or in imagery and painting when other restraints (conscientiousness) weaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of uncultivated/rude energy in the workman
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the chief elements of power in that, and in all good architecture, was the acceptance of uncultivated and rude energy in the workman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor rough, energetic contributions from craftsmen as a source of authenticity and power in Gothic and grotesque expression; 'pride of knowledge' and over-polishing (Renaissance errors) can quench that energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's value tied to expression of personality/soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is valuable or otherwise, only as it expresses the personality, activity, and living perception of a good and great human soul ... and that if it have not this ... it is worthless. Worthless, I mean, as art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge artworks primarily by whether they manifest a living human spirit ('heart-work'); technical finish and scientific accuracy are secondary and cannot substitute for inner expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical fidelity (photographic exactness) is not art
rubrics_metrics.description: For as a photograph is not a work of art ... so, neither would a drawing like a photograph, made directly from nature, be a work of art ... It is no more art to manipulate a camel's hair pencil, than to manipulate a china tray and a glass vial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate high technical skill or faithful literal representation with true artistic value; require interpretation, invention, and the presence of the artist's inner being.
